nom: wet n wild Bare Focus Tinted Hydrator Tinted Skin Veil

segments.oily: Reviewers who describe their skin as oily say the formula does not add extra shine and can be set with a matte powder to tone down its natural dewiness.
segments.dry: Reviewers with dry skin generally find it hydrating and easy to apply over a moisturizer, though a few note it can settle into or highlight dry patches and one calls the base formula itself "quite dry."
segments.combination: Reviewers with combination skin (oily T-zone, drier cheeks) mostly report it blends evenly without separating or breaking them out, but one with sensitive combination skin says it clogged her pores and triggered breakouts.
segments.sensitive: Most reviewers with sensitive skin report no irritation or reaction, including fragrance-free wear on rosacea-prone and acne-prone skin, though a couple describe new breakouts or a greasy-yet-drying feel on eczema-prone cheeks.
segments.normal: One reviewer with normally clear skin says the product caused a significant breakout, while another with normal skin calls it non-comedogenic and praises it highly.
segments.mature: Reviewers in their late 30s to 60s say it does not settle into fine lines or wrinkles and helps cover age-related redness and dark spots, though one in her 50s cautions the formula runs dry so it needs a light hand.

concerns.aging: Reviewers focused on fine lines and wrinkles mostly say the product does not settle into or emphasize them and covers age-related dark spots and uneven texture well; one dissenting review says it visibly filled in and emphasized fine lines when layered over other skincare products.
concerns.dehydration: Reviewers say the hyaluronic-acid formula keeps skin feeling soft and hydrated through the day and does not dry it out; a few dissent, finding it "not very moisturizing" on its own or noting the base formula is "quite dry."
concerns.redness: Reviewers with rosacea or general redness consistently report it visibly reduces and covers redness without irritating their skin; one dissenting review with an active dermatitis flare found it did not minimize the flare's scaly, patchy look.
concerns.barrier: A couple of reviewers with eczema or dermatitis describe the product looking greasy yet feeling drying on affected patches, while another on medication that dries her skin found it did not further clog her already-compromised skin.
concerns.spots: Reviewers say it visibly reduces the look of dark spots, hyperpigmentation and discoloration when built up in layers; one dissent notes it does not fully cover very dark under-eye circles.
concerns.blemishes: Most reviewers with acne-prone or blemish-prone skin report no new breakouts and good coverage of existing spots; three dissenting reviews describe the product itself triggering breakouts or rashy pimples within days, including on skin not normally prone to reacting.
concerns.oiliness: Reviewers, including those with combination or oily skin, mostly say it wears without turning greasy or shiny and can be set with powder to control shine; two dissenting reviews describe it looking or feeling greasy, particularly on reactive or eczema-prone skin.

aspects.libelle: Builds from sheer to medium coverage
Narrow shade range for skin tones
Squeeze tube dispenses too much at once
Strong value for the low price
Lasts most of the day without fading

extraits.texte: When I first tried this product on I really liked it and was very happy with this purchase. I don’t wear makeup often and don’t like a lot of makeup and this was perfect because it made my skin tone even and didn’t look like I was wearing make up. However, after days of using it it made my face break out as shown in the pictures. I have clear skin for the most part. Sometimes I get a pimple here or there but nothing like this. I wash my face every day. I can only gather that this break out is from this product. I’m very disappointed as I really like this product and the way it looks but I can’t have this breakout/rash that this has given me.

extraits.titre: Super thin, not ideal for my skin type
extraits.texte: I've been using the same concealer for years, mainly to even out my tone and cover the occasional blemish, but I thought a tinted serum might be a better option for me now that I'm in my early 40s and prefer minimal makeup. However, this doesn't agree with my sensitive combination skin. It visibly clogs my pores, which makes them stand out more, and it consistently causes breakouts the following day. I used it daily for a fews weeks just to be sure because I do sometimes have such issues for a few days when switching skincare products, but the problem persisted. In general, I find the consistency problematic for me and really don't care for it at all. I expected it to fall somewhere between a creamy moisturizer and a gooey facial serum, but it's actually quite watery and feels very greasy. In addition to my pores, it draws attention to the otherwise inconspicuous fine lines around my eyes by filling them in. I can't say that it has a matte finish as claimed either because it makes my face shiny (and not in that coveted dewy, glowing way). While a tiny amount does a great job of covering up redness, blemishes and dark spots remain completely visible. They can be mildly minimized by applying a bit more, but I really have to fuss to get good results when I try for anything more than super light coverage. Since it's so thin, it never sets like traditional foundation or concealer. A second layer just spreads it all around unevenly. It rubs off on my hands and clothes throughout th

extraits.titre: I was hoping for more based on youtube review
extraits.texte: I have dermatitis on my face which leaves me with patchy, red, dry, flaky areas on my face. While looking for a new tinted moisturizer, I listened to a few reviews on this product, including from someone who has the same skin condition as me. They were happy, so I figured I should try it out. I hardly ever wear make up, but when I do, I wash my face well, and over moisturize. I typically use rosehip oil prior to applying foundation. Then, I always mix a dab of tinted moisturizer to a bigger dab of moisturizer to thin the color and product on my face. I love a very thin translucent layer and dewy skin. When my make up settles, I love to see nothing noticeable in regards to foundation- just smoothed pores and an even skin tone and texture. On areas of my face currently unaffected by dermatitis- although the product looks decent at a semi close distance, when looking closely, the texture left on the face is a bit undesirable. Since using this, I have had peach fuzz, and the product sticks to those hairs and pores. (Often, i like to razor off any peach fuzz on my face for a smooth canvas. ) On this product, I would not recommend using on areas of dermatitis. I have not found any product that can minimize the look of dermatitis during a flare up. In my photo, you can see the areas of dermatitis on my forehead. This is my skin improved SIGNIFICANTLY from the last month. But this is not a product I can use during these flareups without the areas looking scaly. I put a thin layer on

This Wet n Wild Bare Focus Tinted Hydrator is pretty comparable to a CC cream. It’s a combination of a moisturizer and a foundation. I would say it offers light to medium coverage. The finish is dewy. I set mine with a matte powder foundation to tone down the dew because I have oily skin. I ordered the shade “light” for my light skin with golden undertones. It is a little bit dark for me at the moment but will probably be fine in the summer months. This product is very hydrating and stays put. I’m glad it’s so affordable, but don’t know why they charge different amounts depending on the shade. That’s kind of weird. Overall, I think this tinted hydrator is a great value and gives a very effortlessly beautiful look to the skin.

I honestly didn't have super high hopes with this product. Simply because I have very fair, dry, acne prone, sensitive & red skin with crazy under eyes. I wanted a tinted moisturizer that didn't have an SPF, because the SPF always burns my skin, especially my eyes, even if I don't use it anywhere near them. I put this on as soon as I received it and wore it all day at home, just to get an idea of how it looked, felt and lasted on me, as well as any kind of reaction my skin would have to it. I am so pleasantly surprised! It feels like nothing, it applies so well especially over a primer. I use my fingers, as it actually looks better that way. If I have any streaking I just dab it a little with a beauty blender. It also isn't too dark for my skin. I have worn it a few days and haven't had a negative reaction. It looks very natural for me, which is exactly what I've been wanting. It covers/evens out just enough. It also doesn't settle into my lines as much as many other foundation products I've used. I'm not using a powder to set it either. (This photo is really embarrassing for me to post. But, I feel the need to show others.) This is a before and after. All I have on is my normal moisturizer, some ELF power grip primer, the tinted moisturizer, and a little bit of a contour powder on my eyes to avoid any creasing, and a little mascara. It took me 5 minutes to apply this! & I feel so much more confident and put together. I'm buying another one of these tinted moisturizers right

I’ve been using the same foundation for the past 15 years. Unfortunately, they changed the formula a while back and I cant find the best shade match, so I’ve been on the hunt for a new foundation. I have extremely dry cystic acne prone skin. I’m on a host of meds for my skin that only make the dryness worse, so you can imagine trying to find a foundation or skin tint that didn’t just cling to the dry patches and clog my skin more has been a challenge. I’ve watched a zillion tik toks, read a zillion more reviews on Amazon, Google, etc. I’ve not found a single foundation that I felt confident buying. I came across this just scrolling and after reading the reviews and the price point figured I’d give it a try. I am very pale with pink/red undertones and most foundations pull very orange on me so I keep blue foundation handy for mixing. I purchased this in the shade Fair/Pale. Put one pump of my blue in and swirled it around. It went on like butter. You can get some serious coverage with this!! I have only this foundation and some setting powder on in this pic. I did have to go back and add some concealer to my red spots but could probably keep building coverage if I wanted to. It feels like nothing is on my skin! Going back to buy more .

Perfect for subtle rosacea coverup! I have rosacea. (basically dramatic skin redness 24/7) whenever I get warm, or a strong emotion my skin lights up basically like a sunburn. So I want something to make me look somewhat “normal” at work by default and only slightly glowing when I’m getting annoyed. (Ahhh, sweet, sweet retail job) I’ve been wearing this for a couple months now, and I LOVE it. I can apply it in the bathroom in a rush with just my fingers and it melts like butter. And I never noticed and crazy fine lines or spots where the makeup wore off. For reference I’m putting this on at 5am, and taking it off around 9pm. Super recommend for pale rosacea girlies just trying to look more “normal” without feeling like being caked up. I forget I even have this on until I accidentally touch my face.
